the LORD

make two silver trumpets

the door of the tent of meeting

the camps that lie on the south side shall take their journey

to signal preparation for battle only

the first alarm
neither of them

to avoid confusion between arranged trumpet signals (movement signals) and loud shouting that could distract or confuse
because the people would not know how to call at that moment
challenge.explanation: Distinguishing trumpet signals from human shouting prevents confusion: the verse prescribes a clear trumpet signal rather than noisy shouting that could disrupt order.

they mean exactly the same and the verse simply repeats itself
'to blow' means to leap, 'to sound an alarm' means to sing

the whole people
the sons of Aaron the priests

at night before sleeping
only on feast days

in your gladness, in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months
only in the marketplace and in civil assemblies
easy.explanation: Verse 10 lists blowing at days of gladness, appointed feasts, and beginnings of months.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'an ordinance for ever throughout your generations' mean in context?
answers: the law applied only to the first generation
that the practice is permanent and handed down generation to generation
that the trumpets should be preserved as an object only

that a cultic act (blowing) evokes divine remembrance which can result in salvation
that war is an event unrelated to God
challenge.explanation: The verse connects a liturgical act with divine remembrance and ensuing deliverance, indicating theological efficacy of worship.

Reuben

Manasseh

they sang

paragraphs.title: Inviting his father-in-law and his refusal

easy.question: To whom did Moses speak in verse 29?
answers: Hobab son of Raguel the Midianite
to all the men of Israel
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Verse 29 explicitly says Moses spoke to Hobab son of Raguel the Midianite.

easy.question: What did Moses invite Hobab to do in verse 29?
answers: remain and guard the camp
come with us and we will do thee good
return to his country and family
easy.explanation: Moses asked Hobab to 'come thou with us, and we will do thee good' — an invitation to join them.

easy.question: How did Hobab reply in verse 30?
answers: I'll join you after consulting others
I'll serve among you in the wilderness
I will not go; I will return to my own land and to my kindred
easy.explanation: Verse 30 records Hobab's refusal: 'I will not go; but I will depart to mine own land, and to my kindred.'

medium.question: Why does Moses ask Hobab to come with them, according to the verse's wording?
answers: because they were journeying to the land the Lord had promised them
because Moses wanted to part ways with him
because Hobab demanded large payment
medium.explanation: Moses begins by referencing the journey to 'the place which the Lord hath said' — an appeal tied to the destination God promised.

medium.question: What does 'my kindred' mean in Hobab's reply 'to mine own land, and to my kindred'?
answers: rich or fertile land
retirement or pension
his country of birth and relatives
medium.explanation: 'Kindred' here refers to his kin/relatives — the place of his origin and family.

medium.question: What did Moses promise Hobab if he joined them (verse 29)?
answers: to punish him if he betrayed them
they would treat him well and do him good
to give him a miraculous sign
medium.explanation: Moses said 'we will do thee good' — promising kindness and favorable treatment.

challenge.question: What does the term 'father-in-law of Moses' indicate in verse 29?
answers: Moses's father
Moses's brother
Moses's father-in-law (the father of his wife)
challenge.explanation: 'Father-in-law' means the father of one's spouse; Hobab is called Moses' father-in-law.

challenge.question: What can be concluded about Hobab's origin from the verse?
answers: he was a Midianite
he was Egyptian
his origin is not mentioned
challenge.explanation: The verse describes him as 'the Midianite,' indicating Hobab's Midianite origin.

challenge.question: Which detail in Hobab's reply hints at a personal reason for refusing to join the journey?
answers: the reference to the place the Lord promised
his emphasis on 'my land and my kindred', showing ties to his birthplace
the promise Moses made to treat him well
challenge.explanation: Hobab's 'to my own land and to my kindred' stresses personal ties to home and family, explaining his refusal.

questions.question: What does the term 'father-in-law of Moses' indicate in verse 29?
answers: Moses's father
Moses's brother
Moses's father-in-law (the father of his wife)
questions.explanation: 'Father-in-law' means the father of one's spouse; Hobab is called Moses' father-in-law.

answers: he was a Midianite
he was Egyptian
his origin is not mentioned
questions.explanation: The verse describes him as 'the Midianite,' indicating Hobab's Midianite origin.

questions.explanation: Hobab's 'to my own land and to my kindred' stresses personal ties to home and family, explaining his refusal.

easy.question: What do the people ask in verse 31?
answers: that he not leave them
that he lead them alone
that they return to Egypt
easy.explanation: They plead 'I pray thee, leave us not' — asking him to stay with them.

easy.question: What reason do they give in verse 31 for him not to leave them?
answers: because he knows their encampments in the wilderness
because he is great in the law
because they fear another king
easy.explanation: They say 'for thou knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness' — he knows their encamping places.

easy.question: What do they promise to do for him if he goes with them (verse 32)?
answers: to make him king
that if the Lord does well unto us we will do thee good
to abandon him in the wilderness
easy.explanation: They promise 'whatsoever goodness the Lord shall do unto us, the same will we do to thee' — they will repay his help.

medium.question: What does 'if thou go with us' in verse 32 mean in general terms?
answers: that he will remain in place and not travel
that he will travel together with the people
that he will go out to war
medium.explanation: The phrase means to accompany the people on their journey — to travel with them.

medium.question: What does the expression 'to be unto us for eyes' mean in 'thou mayest be to us instead of eyes'?
answers: to be an independent witness
to be a guide or one who knows and shows the way
to be a judge deciding disputes
medium.explanation: It means to act as a guide or eye-witness — someone who knows the routes and helps them navigate.

medium.question: In verse 32, what is meant by 'that which goodness the Lord shall do unto us'?
answers: a specific meal they will give the guide
the blessing the Lord may grant them, which they will reciprocate
an immediate act of service to the leader
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to good that the Lord may do for Israel; in gratitude they will show kindness to him.

challenge.question: What does 'thou knowest our encampments in the wilderness' suggest about the man's relation to the people?
answers: that he has previously been near their encampments and knows the wilderness routes
that he was entirely unknown to them
that their camp never moved from the same place
challenge.explanation: The statement implies prior knowledge of their encampments — he is familiar with their routes and camping spots.

challenge.question: What historical or geographic inference can be drawn from 'our encampments in the wilderness'?
answers: that the people lived in permanent cities in the desert
that the people were nomadic, camping and moving from place to place
that the wilderness had no movement at all
challenge.explanation: Mention of encampments in the wilderness points to a mobile, camp-based lifestyle rather than settled urban living.

challenge.question: What does the promise 'we will do thee good' indicate about the relationship between the people and the man?
answers: a formal commercial contract only
a relationship of rivalry and political pressure
a reciprocal bond of gratitude and support — they will reward his help
challenge.explanation: The promise to repay kindness indicates a reciprocal, supportive relationship and gratitude for his assistance.

answers: that he has previously been near their encampments and knows the wilderness routes

questions.explanation: The promise to repay kindness indicates a reciprocal, supportive relationship and gratitude for his assistance.

paragraphs.title: The ark leads and the cloud accompanies

easy.question: How many days did they journey from the mount of the LORD according to the verse?
answers: three days' journey
one day
seven days
easy.explanation: Verse 33 says 'they departed from the mount of the LORD three days' journey' — three days.

easy.question: What went before them in the three days' journey?
answers: Moses and the people
the ark of the covenant of the LORD
the cloud alone
easy.explanation: The verse notes the ark of the covenant went before them to seek a resting place.

easy.question: What purpose did the ark serve as it went before them?
answers: to provide them food
to fight foreign nations
to search out a resting place for them
easy.explanation: The ark moved ahead 'to search out a resting place for them' — to find where they should encamp.

medium.question: What is likely meant by 'three days' journey' in this context?
answers: the distance to the next stopping place required about three days' travel
that they were forbidden to travel more than a set distance per day
that they had arrived in Canaan after three days
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates the travel to the next resting place required about three days' travel.

medium.question: What does 'resting place' mean in the phrase 'to search out a resting place for them'?
answers: a cult object
a place to halt and stay, a campsite
a promise of future reward
medium.explanation: 'Resting place' refers to a location to stop and encamp — a campsite.

medium.question: What does 'the cloud of the LORD was upon them by day' imply about divine guidance?
answers: the cloud only appeared at night
the cloud never left the camp
the cloud accompanied them in the daytime as a sign of God's presence and guidance
medium.explanation: The cloud's presence by day while they went from the camp shows visible divine guidance during travel.

challenge.question: What practical function did the ark serve when it 'went before them' in biblical tradition?
answers: the ark led and indicated where the next camp should be pitched
the ark served only to store kitchen utensils
the ark always remained in the rear for protection
challenge.explanation: Traditionally the ark signaled the LORD's presence and directed where the people should encamp next.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'to search out a resting place for them' suggest about initiative in guidance?
answers: that the Israelites picked sites without guidance
that God (through the ark/cloud) actively sought out and directed the resting place
that military commanders selected the site
challenge.explanation: The wording implies the divine presence (represented by the ark) took the initiative to find a resting place for the people.

challenge.question: What is the historical meaning of 'the mount of the LORD' in this context?
answers: a general name for any mountain in Canaan
a homeland mountain in the ancient Near East
Mount Sinai — the place where Israel had been when the tabernacle was set up and the law was given
challenge.explanation: 'The mount of the LORD' is traditionally understood as Mount Sinai, where Israel received the law and the tabernacle was located.

questions.explanation: The wording implies the divine presence (represented by the ark) took the initiative to find a resting place for the people.

questions.explanation: 'The mount of the LORD' is traditionally understood as Mount Sinai, where Israel received the law and the tabernacle was located.

easy.question: Who speaks the words in these verses (Numbers 10:35–36)?
answers: Moses
the LORD
the people
easy.explanation: The verses begin 'And Moses said' — Moses is the speaker.

easy.question: When does Moses say 'Rise up, LORD' in the passage?
answers: when the ark set forward (on the move)
when the ark rested
continuously throughout the journey
easy.explanation: Moses says 'Rise up, LORD' as the ark begins to move forward.

easy.question: What does Moses ask when the ark moves, according to the prayer?
answers: that the LORD return to them
that the LORD bless the land
that the LORD scatter his enemies and make them flee
easy.explanation: When the ark sets forward Moses asks 'Rise up, LORD, and let thine enemies be scattered' — that enemies be driven off.

medium.question: What does the word 'return' (as in 'when it rested, he said, Return, O Lord') mean here?
answers: to stay in place
to advance further
to come back and dwell among the great thousands of Israel
medium.explanation: 'Return' here is a plea for the LORD to come back and dwell among the multitudes of Israel.

medium.question: Which phrase is associated with the ark's movement in these verses?
answers: 'Rise up, LORD, and let thine enemies be scattered'
'Return, O Lord, unto thy rest'
'Send us a sign'
medium.explanation: When the ark set forward Moses says 'Rise up, LORD, and let thine enemies be scattered' — that phrase is linked to movement.

medium.question: What does the expression 'many thousands of Israel' indicate in the context?
answers: a small, select group
a very large crowd or multitude of the people
the name of a single tribe
medium.explanation: The phrase denotes a very large number — a vast host of Israel.

challenge.question: When the verse says 'let thine enemies be scattered,' who are meant by 'thy enemies'?
answers: enemies of Moses personally
enemies of the LORD (and thus of Israel)
enemies only of the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Addressed to the LORD, 'thy enemies' refers to the foes of God and therefore of His people.

challenge.question: What functional contrast is expressed by the paired situations 'when it goeth forward' and 'when it resteth' in these verses?
answers: they are merely ceremonial time markers
they are calls to sing only
a distinction of action: when moving Moses prays for enemies to be scattered; when resting he prays for the LORD to return to dwell among Israel
challenge.explanation: The verses set two situations: during movement Moses asks for enemies to be dispersed; at rest he asks the LORD to return to be among the people.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the phrase 'many thousands of Israel' in terms of numerical or rhetorical effect?
answers: an emphasis on a very large multitude
a geographic marker
an emphasis on a small, limited group
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses the great number — 'many thousands' highlights the large scale of Israel's host.
